stories.title: Paper: Player-1 teaches game agents to play from synthetic experience
stories.summary: A new paper introduces Player-1, a method for training game-playing agents on synthetic experience instead of large human demonstration datasets, aiming to extend computer-use agents into visually rich games.
stories.more: The paper argues that while computer-use agents already interpret screens and execute keyboard and mouse actions well, games remain a harder test because of their visual richness and varied mechanics. Existing pipelines for training game agents typically depend on large-scale human demonstrations that cover only a narrow slice of possible game states, and building scalable interactive training environments has been difficult. Player-1 is proposed as a way around this by learning from synthetic experience rather than demonstrations alone. The paper frames this as a step toward more general digital control for AI agents.

stories.title: Paper: ATAS framework keeps long AI-generated videos spatially consistent
stories.summary: Researchers propose Any Time, Any Space (ATAS), a framework that compiles a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and timing so long-form AI video generation stays consistent across nonconsecutive scenes.
stories.more: The paper identifies a gap in current long-form agentic video generation: passing prompts or recent frames between shots doesn't give a model a shared spatial frame to revisit a scene, or a time-indexed record to replay an earlier event. ATAS addresses this by compiling a screenplay into shot requests that carry explicit location, camera, and event-time references. Before generating each shot, the system retrieves relevant context using those references. The approach targets consistency across shots that aren't next to each other in the sequence, a known weak point for video generation models.

stories.title: Paper: LatentLoop scales looped MoE models with asymmetric compute
stories.summary: A new paper studies looped Mixture-of-Experts models that reuse parameters across loop visits, finding the different visits play different roles even though they share weights.
stories.more: Looped MoE models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under a matched compute budget. The paper's authors learn separate residual coefficients for a model that applies a shared block twice, and observe a smaller scale for the first visit than the second. They test fixing those coefficients and find reducing the first visit's scale further changes model behavior. This supports treating loop visits asymmetrically rather than as identical repeated passes.

stories.title: Paper: ActionOPD distills agent decisions instead of tokens
stories.summary: A new paper on distilling language-model agents into smaller models asks at what granularity a student should be aligned with its teacher, proposing decision-level rather than token-level distillation.
stories.more: The paper notes that distilling capable agents into smaller models requires aligning a student's behavior with its teacher's, and that offline imitation offers dense but token-specific supervision that can suffer from state-distribution mismatch. Token-level on-policy distillation addresses some of this, but the paper argues it still misses the right unit of alignment. ActionOPD instead focuses supervision on decisions rather than individual tokens. The excerpt does not detail how much this improves results over token-level approaches.

stories.title: Paper: Cortex consolidates context gains into a model's parameters
stories.summary: A paper proposes Memory Consolidation, which internalizes performance gains from context into a model's own parameters so they survive after the context is removed, inspired by biological memory consolidation.
stories.more: The authors note that context can improve large language model performance, but those gains are typically lost once the context is taken away. Memory Consolidation reframes this as internalizing the gains while preserving the model's other capabilities, linking context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under one objective. The paper introduces a five-task-family test bed to evaluate the approach, though the excerpt does not give specific results.

stories.title: Paper: CriticOPD fixes a flaw in on-policy distillation's teacher supervision
stories.summary: Researchers show that on-policy distillation's assumption, that a teacher can always correct a student's mistakes, fails on wrong rollouts, and propose CriticOPD using error-aware critique to fix it.
stories.more: On-policy distillation trains a student on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes, a property the paper calls recoverability. The authors show this assumption fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher ends up following the student's errors even when it recognizes them as mistakes. CriticOPD is proposed to recover reliable supervision using error-aware critique instead. The excerpt does not specify which benchmarks or models were used to test it.

stories.title: Anthropic details how Claude is being used and guarded around the 2026 midterms
stories.summary: Anthropic published an update on Claude's role in the 2026 US midterms, covering usage data, misuse policies, political-evenhandedness scores, and threats it has detected and blocked.
stories.more: Anthropic says a sample of 250,000 Claude.ai conversations from late September showed about 5.75% touched politics or policy, 0.51% concerned elections, and only about 0.002% violated its election-integrity rules. Claude's latest models scored 99% on the company's political evenhandedness evaluation, though outside reviewers found it sometimes adds unsolicited caveats and hedges unevenly on some topics. Anthropic updated its Usage Policy to ban deceiving voters, and tested safeguards with the Institute for Strategic Dialogue and McCain Institute, finding Claude could miss misuse split into innocuous-looking steps. It also says it banned accounts that used Claude to produce fabricated pro-Russian, Iranian, and North Korean midterm coverage for a foreign-based fake news site.

stories.title: Ricursive Intelligence bets on AI-designed chips to ease the compute crisis
stories.summary: Startup Ricursive Intelligence is developing AI that designs computer chips, learns from each design iteration, and improves future designs, aiming to automate and speed up chip design.
stories.more: According to TechCrunch, the founders describe a closed-loop process where the AI learns from the outcome of each chip iteration to improve the next one. The stated goal is to automate and accelerate chip design as a way to help address the broader AI compute crunch. The excerpt doesn't give funding figures, which chips or customers are involved, or how far along the technology is.

items.title: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis

stories.title: HN: Banks try to offload the AI data center debt they just underwrote
stories.summary: A Hacker News submission highlights banks now trying to offload AI data center debt they recently underwrote themselves, drawing 357 points and 248 comments.
stories.more: The title implies banks took on significant exposure financing AI data center construction and are now looking to reduce or redistribute that risk rather than holding it to maturity. This fits a broader pattern of scrutiny around how AI infrastructure buildouts are being financed. The excerpt doesn't name specific banks, dollar amounts, or which data center projects are involved, only the Hacker News discussion's point and comment counts.
